Per: Justice Avanindra Kumar Singh This criminal appeal under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 07/12/2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Amarwada District Chhindwara (M.P.) in S.C. No.55/2020 (State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Kanhaiya), whereby the appellant has been convicted for offence under Section 366 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 6 months with fine of Rs.500/- and in default further RI for one month and Section 376(3) of Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment further RI for 6 months, with the direction that all the sentences run concurrently.
2.

The minor prosecutrix became pregnant and gave birth to two children.

After the prosecutrix was recovered, she, accused and the born children were subjected to Kanhaiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37913028/

sentences.text:
According to DNA report (Ex.P/24), the prosecutrix (PW-2) is the mother and appellant is the father of the children.
4.
As per prosecution, regarding the incident missing person report No.11/2015 (Ex.P/16) was recorded and when prosecutrix was recovered, then FIR (Ex.P/17) was registered against the appellant/accused.
After completing the investigation, charge-sheet has been filed against the appellant.
5. The trial Court charged the accused for the offences as mentioned in Para-1 of the judgment.
The accused denied the charges and sought trial.
It is to be further noted that the trial Court has also charged the accused under Section 344 of Indian Penal Code but after the trial, appellant was acquitted for the same charges.
6. Prosecution has recorded the evidence.
In examination under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. accused again denied that he abducted the minor prosecutrix.
He stated that he is innocent but admitted that prosecutrix and her father, mother are known to him.
It is also admitted that he is the husband of prosecutrix NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36375 3 CRA-98-2024 (PW-2) and children are born out of his relationship with prosecutrix.
They are his children.
Prosecutrix was recovered from his custody.

He also admitted the DNA report in answer to question no.55.
7.
Against the judgment of conviction and sentence, appeal has been filed on the ground that the trial Court has not properly dealt with the evidence.
No charges were proved against the accused/appellant.
Prosecution evidence is not reliable therefore appellant may be acquitted.
It is pertinent to note that appellant has not produced any defence witness.
8. Shri Arvind Singh, learned Government advocate for the State supports the impugned judgment and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
9. In the backdrop of admission of the accused, the question which arises for decision of this appeal is whether the prosecutrix was major on the date of incident ?

10. Mother of the prosecutrix (PW-1) in her statement stated that they have lodged missing person report and her daughter was recovered from the possession of the appellant/accused but she was declared hostile by the prosecution.
In answer to leading question, she did not stated any word in favour of the prosecutrix.

In cross-examination by the defence, she has stated that she does not know the age of the prosecutrix because she was illiterate and the school teacher recorded the date of birth of the prosecutrix by their own will.
11. Prosecutrix (PW-2) in examination-in-chief has stated that she married the accused in the year 2016 and she has two children from the marital relationship with the accused.
This witness is also declared hostile.
In answer to leading question by the prosecution, this witness has stated that the age NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36375 4 CRA-98-2024 recorded in marksheet is wrong.
She admitted that when she was 8 years she had gone to school for the first time.
This witness has not supported the case of the prosecution.

While in examination by defence, she stated Kanhaiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37913028/
2 that when she went to get admission then school teacher asked for catching hold her ear and she was admitted on the same ground.

entities.text: Kanhaiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
She also admitted that she went away with accused after she had attained the age of 18 years.
12.

Head Master (PW-3) had stated that in Dakhila Kharij Register (Ex.P/6) date of birth of the prosecutrix is recorded as 08/05/2002 but in para-3 of his cross-examination, he stated that he cannot say on what basis, the date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded.

He further stated that they cross check the birth date from the Kotwar register and Aaganwadi register and if there is no record as such, they ask the student to catch the left ear from the right hand over the head then he record the age by estimation.
In this case, no record of Kotwar register or Aaganwadi register has been filed.
13. Father of the prosecutrix (PW-7) has also turned hostile.
Although he has stated that he lodged missing person report (Ex.P/16) and FIR (Ex.P/17) but the prosecution has declared hostile this witness also.
In answer to leading question, he has not supported the prosecution case.

In cross- examination by defence, he has stated that while getting the admission of the prosecutrix in the school, he has not given any document in support of date of birth and the date of birth has been mentioned in the register only on estimation.
In para-8 he has further submitted that he does not know the date of birth of his other children.
14. Dr. Anju Tyagi (PW-9) stated that when she examined the prosecutrix, she did not found any injury on her internal or external parts of the body.

In NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:36375 5 CRA-98-2024 para-2 of her cross-examination, while she examined the prosecutrix she found that prosecutrix was fully adult.

15. Considering the arguments of learned counsel for both the parties and on going through the oral and documentary evidence, it is found that the trial Court has erred in recording the finding in Para 16 of the impugned judgment that on the date of incident i.e. on 15/04/2015 prosecutrix was minor.
On the contrary, it is found that prosecution has failed to prove that on the date of incident the prosecutrix was minor.

Accordingly, this finding of the trial Court that on the date of incident prosecutrix was minor is set aside and having set aside this finding in light of evidence of this case,
no offence would be made out against the appellant/accused for which he has been convicted and sentenced by the impugned judgment because any relationship between appellant and prosecutrix in this case cannot be given a stamp of a crime.
16. In view of the aforesaid, the impugned judgment dated 07/12/2023 passed in Case No.55/2020 is set aside.
The appeal filed by the appellant is hereby allowed and disposed of.
17. The appellant be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
The case property be disposed off as per Para-50 of the judgment of the trial Court.
Record of the trial Court be sent back.
